prompt: A company based in Portugal sells vitamins online to customers in Brazil. Does the LGPD apply to it?

choices.text: Yes; it offers goods to people in Brazil
choices.why: Right. Where the company sits does not decide it.

choices.text: No, because it is not established in Brazil
choices.why: No. Article 3 reaches offers aimed at people in Brazil.

choices.text: Only if its servers are in Brazil
choices.why: No. Where the servers are is not the test.

choices.text: Only for customers who pay in reais
choices.why: No. The currency has nothing to do with it.

prompt: Match each article of the LGPD to what it is about.
hint: The map on the first page of the lesson.

prompt: Ipê keeps the date of birth of every customer "in case it is useful one day". Which principle of article 6 does that break first?

choices.text: Transparency
choices.why: No. Telling the customer would not make the purpose any more specific.

choices.text: Security
choices.why: No. The data can be perfectly secure and still have no reason to be there.

choices.text: Purpose
choices.why: Right. Processing needs a specific, explicit purpose decided beforehand.

choices.text: Non-discrimination
choices.why: No. Nobody is being treated differently yet.

prompt: Which principle asks the controller to be able to show, with evidence, that it complies?

choices.text: Quality of the data, because evidence is data
choices.why: No. Quality is about the data being accurate and current.

choices.text: Free access, since the data subject can check
choices.why: No. Free access is the person's right to consult their data.

choices.text: Prevention, which covers every measure taken beforehand
choices.why: No. Prevention is about avoiding damage, not demonstrating compliance.

choices.text: Accountability
choices.why: Right. Responsabilização e prestação de contas: showing, not only doing.

prompt: Match each of Ipê's purposes to the legal basis it rests on.

pairs.left: the address to deliver an order

prompt: A customer withdraws consent to marketing. What happens to Ipê's use of their e-mail for delivery notices?
hint: A basis belongs to a purpose.

choices.text: It must stop, since the column is now without consent
choices.why: No. Delivery notices never rested on consent.

choices.text: It goes on, under the contract
choices.why: Right. Only the purpose that rested on consent stops.

choices.text: It goes on only if the customer consents again
choices.why: No. The contract is the basis; consent was never needed for it.

choices.text: The e-mail must be deleted within 15 days
choices.why: No. Withdrawing consent is not a request to delete everything.

prompt: How many legal bases does article 7 of the LGPD list for personal data?
Ipê wants to e-mail customers who bought diabetes products about a new glucose meter. Which basis is available?
hint: What does the purchase reveal, and which article governs that?

choices.text: Specific, highlighted consent for that purpose
choices.why: Right. Article 11, I: consent given in a specific and highlighted way.

choices.text: Legitimate interest, because they are existing customers
choices.why: No. Article 11 has no legitimate interest for sensitive data.

choices.text: Protecting health, since the meter helps them
choices.why: No. That basis is for health professionals and services, not for sales.

choices.text: Performing a contract, the earlier purchase
choices.why: No. The earlier sale does not cover a new offer.

prompt: Which basis lets the pharmacist check a prescription at the counter without asking the customer for consent?

choices.text: Legitimate interest of the pharmacy
choices.why: No. It is not available for sensitive data.

choices.text: None; a prescription always needs consent
choices.why: No. Article 11, II lists bases without consent.

choices.text: Protecting health, by a health professional
choices.why: Right. Tutela da saúde, in a procedure by a health professional.

choices.text: Protecting credit, since the order is paid
choices.why: No. Credit protection is not a basis in article 11.

prompt: Why did Ipê replace `marketing_opt_in boolean` with a table of consent events?

choices.text: Booleans are slow to index in PostgreSQL
choices.why: No. Speed has nothing to do with it.

choices.text: Because the law forbids storing a person's consent in a boolean column
choices.why: No. The law asks for proof, not for a particular table.

choices.text: To let customers consent on behalf of others
choices.why: No. Nothing in the design does that.

choices.text: To prove what was consented to, and when it was withdrawn
choices.why: Right. The burden of proof is on the controller.

prompt: After customer 1 withdrew, how many customers had a standing marketing consent?
Article 8, §4: authorisations that are ___ are void; consent must refer to determined purposes.
In the balancing test, what does the question "would the person reasonably expect this?" weigh?
hint: Whose side of the scale is it on?

choices.text: Whether the purpose itself is lawful and concrete enough
choices.why: No. That is the first question, about the controller.

choices.text: Whether the person's rights prevail
choices.why: Right. Expectations are on the person's side of the scale.

choices.text: Whether the same purpose could be met with less data
choices.why: No. That is necessity, the second question.

choices.text: Which safeguards to adopt
choices.why: No. Safeguards are the fourth question.

prompt: Put the four questions of a legitimate interest assessment in order.
hint: From the controller's purpose to the person's protection.

prompt: Match each request to the right of article 18 it exercises.

pairs.left: "Send me everything you hold about me"
"Who did you give my data to?"

prompt: Ipê corrected a customer's address and had shared it with a delivery company. What does article 18, §6 ask?

choices.text: Telling the delivery company, so it corrects it too
choices.why: Right. The controller passes the correction on.

choices.text: Nothing more; the correction is done in Ipê's database
choices.why: No. The other agent still holds the old address.

choices.text: Asking the customer to contact the delivery company
choices.why: No. The duty is the controller's, not the person's.

choices.text: Charging the customer for the second correction
choices.why: No. Requests cost the person nothing (§5).

prompt: A fraud model cancels a customer's order with no person involved. What can the customer ask for under article 20?

choices.text: Nothing, since fraud detection rests on legitimate interest
choices.why: No. The basis does not remove the right to a review.

choices.text: A review that by law must be done by a person
choices.why: No. The 2019 reform left "by a natural person" out.

choices.text: A review, and the criteria the decision used
choices.why: Right. Article 20 and its §1, trade secrets protected.

choices.text: The model's source code and training data
choices.why: No. Trade and industrial secrets are protected.

prompt: Davi's role had `SELECT` on `sales.customers`. Why did it also need a policy?
hint: Lesson 2 turned something on in that table.

choices.text: Without one, the query fails with a permission denied error on the table
choices.why: No. It returns zero rows and no error, which is worse.

choices.text: Policies are needed to read encrypted columns
choices.why: No. Decryption happens in OpenBao, not in a policy.

choices.text: `SELECT` alone lets the role change rows
choices.why: No. `SELECT` reads; it changes nothing.

choices.text: Row-level security returns no rows to a role with no policy
choices.why: Right. And the export would have come back empty, silently.

prompt: How does `export_subject.py` decide which tables to read?

choices.text: A list of tables written at the top of the script
choices.why: No. A list would miss the next table somebody adds.

choices.text: `gov.column_class`: tables with `customer_id`, or `order_id` and no `customer_id`
choices.why: Right. A newly classified table is in the export with no edit.

choices.text: Every table in the database that Davi can read
choices.why: No. Most of them are not about a customer.

choices.text: The foreign keys pointing at `sales.customers`
choices.why: No. Order items reach a customer through an order, not by a key to customers.

prompt: Within how many days must a complete declaration of access be given, under article 19?
Why is `due_on` a generated column instead of a value typed in when the request arrives?
hint: What could two columns do that one cannot?

choices.text: So it cannot disagree with `received_on`
choices.why: Right. One fact, one source.

choices.text: Generated columns use less disk
choices.why: No. A stored generated column takes the same space.

choices.text: Because the law forbids editing a deadline
choices.why: No. The law says nothing about columns.

choices.text: So that Davi can extend it when needed
choices.why: No. A generated column cannot be written at all.

prompt: Customer 3 asked for deletion. Which of their data did Ipê delete or replace? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: The support tickets
choices.why: They served only the relationship.

choices.text: The e-mail address
choices.why: Replaced by an address that cannot receive mail.

choices.text: The orders
choices.why: Kept under article 16, I, for tax law.

choices.text: The prescriptions
choices.why: Kept under article 16, I, for the health authority.

choices.text: The consent events
choices.why: Kept as proof; a withdrawal event was added.

prompt: Why did Ipê replace customer 3's e-mail instead of deleting the customer row?

choices.text: Deleting rows is forbidden by the LGPD
choices.why: No. The law asks for deletion; it does not forbid it.

choices.text: To be able to send the customer a confirmation of the deletion later on
choices.why: No. The new address cannot receive mail.

choices.text: Kept orders point at it, and the e-mail was not needed for them
choices.why: Right. The row stays for what must stay; the e-mail goes.

choices.text: Because the e-mail is sensitive data
choices.why: No. An e-mail is personal, not sensitive.

prompt: After the transaction, customer 3's tickets are still in last week's backup. What is the defensible practice?

choices.text: Edit every backup to remove them
choices.why: No. Editing backups breaks what makes them backups.

choices.text: Nothing, since backups are outside the law
choices.why: No. A backup is processing like any other.

choices.text: Tell the customer the deletion is impossible
choices.why: No. The deletion was done; backups follow it.

choices.text: Let them expire on schedule, and re-delete on any restore
choices.why: Right. Out of normal use, and the deletion re-applied if restored.

prompt: Article 38 lets the ANPD require the controller to prepare a data protection ___ assessment, the RIPD.
How many of Ipê's 6,012 customers have at least one prescription on file?
Why does Ipê compute the facts of its RIPD with a query?

choices.text: Because the ANPD accepts an impact report only when it is written as SQL
choices.why: No. The ANPD accepts a document.

choices.text: A measured fact is rerun and checked; a remembered one is not
choices.why: Right. And it found two findings on the way.

choices.text: So that the report can be finished without listing any residual risks
choices.why: No. A report that lists none has not looked.

choices.text: Queries replace the measures section
choices.why: No. The measures still need describing, with their evidence.

prompt: Under Resolução CD/ANPD 15/2024, within how many working days must the controller notify the ANPD of an incident with relevant risk?
From when does the communication deadline count?
hint: Not from the end of anything.

choices.text: From when the controller knows personal data was affected
choices.why: Right. The clock starts on knowledge, not certainty.

choices.text: From the end of the investigation
choices.why: No. That is why the information can be completed later.

choices.text: From when the press or a customer first reports the incident in public
choices.why: No. Publicity has nothing to do with it.

choices.text: From when whoever caused it has been identified and stopped by the team
choices.why: No. Who caused it may never be identified.

prompt: Put an incident's milestones in the order the regulation sets them.
items: The controller learns personal data was affected
The ANPD and the people affected are notified
The record's five years run out

prompt: What is the ceiling of a simple fine under article 52?

choices.text: 4% of worldwide turnover
choices.why: No. That is the GDPR's ceiling.

choices.text: R$ 50 million per year, whatever the revenue
choices.why: No. The cap is per infraction, and the 2% comes first.

choices.text: 2% of revenue in Brazil, up to R$ 50 million per infraction
choices.why: Right. Net of taxes, for the last financial year.

choices.text: A fixed table of amounts per article broken
choices.why: No. The dosimetry regulation calculates it case by case.

prompt: Ipê appoints an outside firm as encarregado. Who answers to the ANPD for complying with the LGPD?

choices.text: The outside firm, which now holds the role
choices.why: No. The appointment does not move the responsibility.

choices.text: The two of them in equal shares, by contract
choices.why: No. A contract cannot move the law's responsibility.

choices.text: Each data subject's own lawyer
choices.why: No. Data subjects are owed the duty, not given it.

choices.text: Ipê, the controller
choices.why: Right. The responsibility stays with the controller.

prompt: Match each situation at Ipê to the article that answers it.

pairs.left: A customer asks to be deleted
The fraud model cancels an order

prompt: Request 3 was received on 10 June and is unanswered on 1 July. What did the lab use to find it?

choices.text: A complaint from the customer to the ANPD
choices.why: No. The query found it before any complaint.

choices.text: A query comparing `due_on` with today
choices.why: Right. A deadline in a table can be checked every morning.

choices.text: Davi's calendar reminder
choices.why: No. The deadline lives in the table.

choices.text: An index on `received_on`
choices.why: No. An index makes a query fast; it finds nothing alone.
